title: References & Glossary
summary: Every source, every claim, and every term used on this site — and how each figure was checked.

sections.heading: Why only standards bodies, regulators and peer-reviewed research
sections.body:
This site informs decisions about hospital infrastructure, so every technical figure comes from the organisations that define Wi-Fi and its rules: IEEE, the Wi-Fi Alliance, IETF and national regulators such as the FCC. Healthcare context may also draw on peer-reviewed research and health authorities.

We never cite vendor material, Wikipedia, blogs, forums, news or AI-generated text — if one of those points to a useful fact, we find and cite the original source instead.

sections.heading: How each figure is recorded and checked
sections.body:
Every number or rule on the site is a **claim** that records its source, the exact clause, table or page, and how the value was obtained: **stated** in the source, **derived** from other cited values (for example, peak rates are recalculated from the standard's parameters every time the site is built), or **illustrative** (a picture of a pattern, with no numbers shown).

A reviewer checks each claim against its source and records the date and their initials; claims must be re-checked at least every 12 months. Select any small number in brackets, or any key figure, to see this for yourself.

sections.heading: What the labels mean
sections.body:
**Theoretical maximum** — the highest value the standard allows with every option at its limit; real devices and real networks achieve less.

**In the standard; not in current devices** — defined by IEEE but beyond what shipping devices implement.

**Varies by country** — depends on national radio rules; the region used is named.

**Illustrative** — shows the shape of an effect, not measured values.
